events.subtitle: The Last Farewell Tour

priority_review.rationale: Concrete scarcity is the farewell condition itself: Billboard JAPAN's official tour page says Little Feat are drawing a line under more than half a century of live touring, and January 6 is the only announced Tokyo/Kanto performance in the Japan routing. A+ was explicitly challenged and judged insufficient because a future routine Tokyo return cannot reasonably be assumed once the band has announced the end of touring; missing this date could therefore create genuine regret. S+ is not warranted because Tachikawa is not advertised as the band's singular final concert: the Japan run also includes Osaka on January 4 and The Last Farewell Tour is a broader routing. This is a protect-the-night final-access event, not an alter-plans historically unique last show.

events.factual_description: Billboard JAPAN presents Little Feat's The Last Farewell Tour at Tachikawa Stage Garden on Wednesday, January 6, 2027, with doors at 18:00 and the performance at 19:00. The official Japan tour page describes the run as the band bringing more than half a century of live touring to a close and lists the Japan-performance personnel as Bill Payne, Kenny Gradney, Fred Tackett, Scott Sharrard and Tony Leone. It announces two Japan dates: Osaka Festival Hall on January 4 and Tachikawa Stage Garden on January 6. Published Tokyo ticket categories are meet-and-greet VIP ¥50,000, front SS reserved ¥18,900, S reserved ¥16,800, A reserved ¥15,800 and third-floor U25 ¥8,900. Because the event-specific Japan page does not list Sam Clayton in its MEMBER section, he is not inferred into this performance lineup despite appearing among current band members on Little Feat's own site.

enrichment.note: Date, doors, showtime, venue, published Japan-tour personnel, farewell context, two-date Japan routing, published ticket categories, an authorized ticket destination and an exact Apple Music album destination are verified. No unannounced personnel, repertoire or additional Japan dates are inferred.

Official band site verifies the current band identity and member roster. It includes Sam Clayton, who is intentionally not added to this event's lineup because the event-specific Japan tour page lists only Payne, Gradney, Tackett, Sharrard and Leone.

en.why_it_matters: Little Feat's farewell matters because the thing disappearing is precisely what made the band consequential: a live, elastic groove where rock, New Orleans rhythm, blues, funk and jazz could coexist without sounding stitched together. Tachikawa is the only announced Tokyo/Kanto stop in the two-date Japan run, so this is not a generic legacy booking but a finite chance to hear that language from the band that spent decades refining it onstage.
en.trip_verdict: If Tokyo/Kanto is already part of January, protect January 6 and let Tachikawa anchor the evening. From the DMV, I would not build an entire Japan trip around this one stop alone unless Little Feat is personally central, because the farewell routing includes other cities; within Japan, however, this is the Kanto date to choose.

es.why_it_matters: La despedida de Little Feat importa porque lo que desaparece es justamente aquello que volvió esencial a la banda en vivo: un groove flexible donde rock, ritmo de Nueva Orleans, blues, funk y jazz conviven sin sentirse pegados a la fuerza. Tachikawa es la única fecha anunciada en Tokio/Kanto dentro de las dos presentaciones japonesas, así que no es una escala rutinaria de una banda histórica sino una oportunidad finita de escuchar ese lenguaje en manos del grupo que pasó décadas afinándolo sobre el escenario.
es.trip_verdict: Si Tokio/Kanto ya forma parte del plan de enero, protegería el 6 de enero y dejaría que Tachikawa ancle la noche. Desde el DMV no armaría un viaje completo a Japón únicamente por esta escala salvo que Little Feat sea personalmente central, porque la despedida recorre otras ciudades; dentro de Japón, en cambio, ésta es la fecha de Kanto que escogería.
